test_title: SSC CGL (2022) Tier-II Official Paper (Held On : 7 March 2023)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution:
Here the correct answer is **Cultures.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer for **blank number 2 **is** 3) cultures.**
 
• The phrase **"in cultures" **refers to various societies or civilizations around the world.
 
• In this context, it indicates that the Sun holds significance in the mythologies and religions of different cultures.
 
 
• "The Sun has inspired us since ancient times. It’s central to mythology and religion **in cultures__ **around the world."
 
 
 
• This means that the Sun has played a significant role in the beliefs, stories, and religious practices of various societies throughout history.
 
• Using **"scenes" (option 1) **would imply specific locations or settings where the Sun is observed, which is not the intended meaning in this context.
 
• Using **"processes" (option 2) **would suggest that the Sun is central to certain natural processes, which is not the main focus of the sentence.
 
• Using** "types" (option 4) **would not convey the intended meaning as it does not accurately describe the broad range of cultures being referred to.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **3) cultures**, as it appropriately indicates the diversity of societies and their beliefs related to the Sun.

__Correct Paragraph__: *The Sun is the star at the center of (1) __the__ Solar System. It is a nearly perfect ball of hot plasma. The Sun has inspired us since ancient times. It’s central to mythology and religion in **(2) __cultures__** around the world. It keeps our planet warm enough for living things to grow. It gives us light so we can see. It is by far the most important (3) _________of energy for life on Earth. It is about a hundred times as wide (4)________ the Earth. If there were no sun, many things wouldn’t occur like photosynthesis or the presence of oxygen, which would have caused no existence of life.*
